signal.summary: The Argentine Peso (ARS) faces mild short-term macro pressure due to market expectations of nominal depreciation from the current spot level of 1505 ARS/USD towards 1530.40 in September and 1565 in October, along with expected monthly CPI inflation of 1.8%. This pressure is partially mitigated by BCRA's reaffirmed fiscal and monetary inflation anchors and reported past FX reserve accumulation.

factors.reason: BCRA reaffirmed its fiscal and monetary inflation anchor and reported USD 13,337 million in cumulative FX purchases through July 31.
REM survey participants project ARS nominal depreciation to 1530.40 in September and 1565 in October, with expected monthly CPI inflation of 1.8%.
Official spot proxy recorded at 1505 ARS per USD, showing relatively stable short-term movement (+0.33% 7-day change, -0.66% 30-day change).

explanation.approximation: MONTHLY_AVERAGE forecast used unchanged as a 30-day proxy; no interpolation, annualization or time scaling. Representative horizon 41.49999999421296 days from spot observation.

signal.summary: BRL benefits from strong carry support driven by a high 14% Selic policy rate alongside subdued near-term inflation (IPCA July at 0.07% and IPCA-15 August at -0.40%). This provides high real interest rates. Moderate counter-pressure comes from Focus survey expectations predicting slight depreciation toward 5.20 BRL/USD by October 2026.

factors.reason: The Selic target rate stands at 14.0% per annum, offering substantial nominal yield support for BRL against USD.
August IPCA-15 preview registered at -0.40%, indicating near-term deflationary pressure that increases real yield buffers.
July IPCA showed monthly inflation of 0.07% and 12-month inflation of 4.44%, reinforcing positive real interest rates.
Focus survey medians project monthly average PTAX of 5.18 BRL/USD in Sept 2026 and 5.20 in Oct 2026, implying expected currency depreciation from current spot levels.
Spot rate of 5.1114 reflects minor 7-day depreciation (+0.60%) alongside 30-day gain (-0.60%).

signal.summary: Brazilian Real (BRL) benefits from strong macro fundamentals in the short term. The central bank maintains a high policy Selic rate of 14.0% per annum, while August IPCA data registered deflation of -0.32% (bringing 12-month inflation down to 4.22%). This combination boosts real yields substantially, offering robust carry support against the USD. However, BCB Focus survey expectations signal potential mild exchange rate depreciation toward 5.20 BRL/USD by October 2026 compared to the current spot level of 5.1108.

factors.reason: The Selic target rate stands at 14.0% per annum, maintaining a significant interest rate differential that supports carry demand for BRL.
August IPCA inflation dropped by -0.32% monthly and 12-month inflation slowed to 4.22%, widening Brazil's real interest rate margin.
Market participants in the Focus survey expect monthly average PTAX to weaken slightly to 5.18 in September and 5.20 BRL/USD in October 2026 relative to current spot levels.
Spot FX observed at 5.1108 BRL/USD reflects a 7-day BRL appreciation of approximately 0.72%.

explanation.approximation: MONTHLY_AVERAGE forecast used unchanged as a 30-day proxy; no interpolation, annualization or time scaling. Representative horizon 35.49999999421296 days from spot observation.
